issues.issue: Broad all-funds group, not an unexplained 'Miscellaneous' line. The p4 and p6 statements show it is mostly charges for services: business-type charges 3,486,213 + fees 65,309 + governmental charges 40,136 = about 3.59M of 4.55M. The mixed-line rule calls for the dominant category ('charges for services/fees', detail 'other charges for services') with review naming the mix, not 'other'.

issues.on_page: Public Safety 431,960; Culture and Recreation 742,569; Community Development 16,706; Public Works - other 27,906; Capital outlay 484,203; revenues 365,031; transfers 1,233,513
issues.issue: Double counting across schedules. The other-governmental-funds amounts on p8 are already inside the all-funds budget schedule lines on p7. For example, Public Safety 431,960 is in both detail[10] and detail[25], and Community Development 16,706 in both detail[14] and detail[27]. The extractor's notes admit the overlap, but the no-double-counting rule allows only one schedule's lines for the same funds.

The all-funds schedule mixes fund types. 'Other local receipts' 4,548,147 includes about 3.59M of business-type revenue, 'Transfers in' 1,849,554 (detail[8]) includes 266,700 business-type, and 'Culture and Recreation' 949,032 (detail[13]) may include golf. All of these are tagged governmental, so governmental detail is overstated. The schedule can't be split by fund, so this is a limitation, not a misread.

issues.on_page: Other revenue 269,024 (p8 combining: Keno Fund 41,354, Fire Fund 115,731, Sales Tax Fund 9,588, Pool 9,259...)
issues.issue: The combining schedule shows part of this line by fund: 41,354 is in the Keno Fund (probably keno/lottery) and 115,731 in the Fire Fund (probably rural fire contracts or charges). The label gives no breakdown, so 'other' with review is defensible. The same applies to detail[24].

Every business-type expense line is tagged 'utilities', including the Golf Course Fund's 359,057, which is culture/recreation. The statement lists spending by object, so this is a judgment call. It applies to disbursements[9]-[17].
